problem: Suppose that $f(x)$ is a function such that ${\int }_{8}^{5}3f(x)\,\text{d}x=-2$ and ${\int }_{3}^{5}f(x)\,\text{d}x=-3.$ What is the value of ${\int }_{3}^{8}f(x)\,\text{d}x?$

feedback.problem: Suppose that $f(x)$ is a  function such that ${\int }_{2}^{6}f(x)\,\text{d}x=9$ and ${\int }_{9}^{6}4\,f(x)\,\text{d}x=20.$ What is the value of ${\int }_{2}^{9}f(x)\,\text{d}x?$
feedback.worked_solution:
Let's simplify one of the given integrals:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{9}^{6}4\,f(x)\,\text{d}x & =20 \\ 4{\int }_{9}^{6}\,f(x)\,\text{d}x & =20 \\ -4{\int }_{6}^{9}f(x)\,\text{d}x & =20 \\ {\int }_{6}^{9}f(x)\,\text{d}x & =-5\end{aligned}
$$

Then, from the adjacent intervals rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{2}^{9}f(x)\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{2}^{6}f(x)\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{6}^{9}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =9+(-5) \\  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$
